Platform: VolunteerU
Nonprofit organization: HerWell Community Alliance

September Board and Program Planning
HerWell Community Alliance
SYNTHETIC DEMO ONLY — fictional organization, people, schools, venues, and records.
Meeting date: 2026-09-10 | Time zone: America/New_York
Format: fictional AI meeting summary and timestamped transcript; not an export from a real note-taking service.

Summary
Board planning established two November events, four program categories, 100 needed student places, a 150-person recruitment target, October outreach, and a December review. Procurement and student assignments require confirmation.

Transcript

[00:00] Susie Bennett | Executive Director
We are planning two November events under HerWell Community Alliance. Our four categories are period health, cancer support, maternal health, and mental health. October is recruitment month. Today is planning, not authorization for the AI to send messages or assign people.

[01:15] Jane Ellis | Board Chair
Approve the event concept and a combined 100 student shift places. Our outreach target is 150 unique students, but that is a recruitment goal, not a confirmed roster. Each student should hold one primary event shift in this demo.

[02:30] Manny Cruz | Volunteer Coordinator
Event E001, HerWell Community Care Day, is November 14 at the fictional Cypress Community Garden in Broward. It is outdoors. We need 60 students: setup 12, period health kit packing 14, maternal health supplies 12, welcome and wayfinding 10, and cleanup 12. Setup starts at 6:30 a.m.; public hours are 9 a.m. to noon.

[04:10] Priya Shah | Programs Lead
Event E002, HerWell Support and Connection Fair, is November 21 at the fictional Bayview Community Hall in Miami-Dade. We need 40 students: setup 8, cancer support resource packs 10, mental health welcome desk 10, and cleanup 12. Setup starts at 8 a.m.; public hours are 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Students support logistics; qualified staff handle counseling and health questions.

[06:00] Lena Brooks | Logistics Lead
I can request 20 tables, 60 chairs, two banners, four canopies, and drinking water for E001. That is a request, not a supplier confirmation. I will get quantities and delivery windows by September 24. E002 needs 12 tables and 40 chairs; the venue inventory is still unconfirmed.

[07:40] Jane Ellis | Board Chair
Lena, please also obtain an indoor backup quote for the outdoor event. Susie will approve the final weather contingency by October 23. Do not assume we already booked a backup venue.

[09:10] Amina Cole | Grants and Evaluation Lead
I need counts of registered students, unique attendees, approved hours, and resource packs distributed by category for the December 4 review. Registration is not attendance. Keep supply outputs separate from volunteer hours and do not put recipient names or medical details in student notes.

[10:45] Diego Rivera | Communications Lead
I will draft the October campaign by September 28. We will share links by website, email, LinkedIn, Eventbrite, and Luma, plus school invitations. Every link should open our central signup form with a campaign tag. We are not claiming live imports from those services.

[12:20] Manny Cruz | Volunteer Coordinator
Schools will create VolunteerU accounts and receive school-specific invitation links. Students select high school, undergraduate, or graduate, enter their required hours and deadline, and give available days, time windows, interests, and role preferences. School requirements come from the school account; extra personal targets can be separate.

[14:05] Susie Bennett | Executive Director
Manny, send school onboarding information by September 25 after I approve the draft. Before assigning students, check availability, age restrictions, consent, and training. Students under 18 need recorded guardian consent and an adult lead. Do not assign clinical work.

[15:30] Manny Cruz | Volunteer Coordinator
I will propose shifts after recruitment. The AI may draft tasks with an owner, deadline, and transcript evidence. I approve assignments and outgoing reminders. If a deadline is missing, flag it instead of making one up.

[17:00] Priya Shah | Programs Lead
If a family leaves without a kit, the volunteer can record an anonymous operational concern and notify the staff lead. They should not diagnose the reason. We need the coordinator to review service issues before treating them as resolved.

[18:30] Susie Bennett | Executive Director
Decisions confirmed: two events, 100 planned shift places, October recruitment, and December 4 review. Supply orders, backup venue, student assignments, and reminders remain pending the responsible person’s confirmation.

End of mock transcript. Task extraction is intentionally left for the platform AI; the discussion contains confirmed decisions, commitments, tentative suggestions, and unresolved items.

Platform: VolunteerU
Nonprofit organization: HerWell Community Alliance

September Volunteer Operations and Outreach
HerWell Community Alliance
SYNTHETIC DEMO ONLY — fictional organization, people, schools, venues, and records.
Meeting date: 2026-09-24 | Time zone: America/New_York
Format: fictional AI meeting summary and timestamped transcript; not an export from a real note-taking service.

Summary
Operations confirmed table and chair quantities, defined shifts, school onboarding, source tracking, deduplication, and approval rules. Canopies, weather backup, and optional purchases remain unresolved.

Transcript

[00:00] Manny Cruz | Volunteer Coordinator
This is our operations follow-up for the November 14 and November 21 events. School outreach opens October 1 and closes October 31. We still target 150 unique students against 100 needed places. The actual roster may be smaller.

[01:20] Lena Brooks | Logistics Lead
The supplier confirmed 20 tables and 60 chairs for E001, arriving November 14 at 6 a.m. The two banners are ordered for November 6 delivery. Canopies are still pending; do not mark them received. E002 confirmed 12 tables and 40 chairs in the hall.

[03:00] Manny Cruz | Volunteer Coordinator
E001 shifts are setup 06:30–09:00, period health kit packing 08:30–12:00, maternal health supplies 08:30–12:00, welcome and wayfinding 08:30–12:00, and cleanup 12:00–14:00. E002 shifts are setup 08:00–10:00, cancer support resource packs 09:30–13:00, mental health welcome desk 09:30–13:00, and cleanup 13:00–15:00. All times are America/New_York.

[05:10] Priya Shah | Programs Lead
Keep the planned role counts from September 10. Period kits need inventory labels; maternal supplies need size checks. Cancer support volunteers assemble resource packs and guide visitors to staff. The mental health welcome desk handles directions and materials only, with no counseling or collection of health histories.

[06:50] Diego Rivera | Communications Lead
Campaign drafts are ready. Susie, please review them by September 28 so we can publish October 1. I will label referral channels separately from registration systems. A LinkedIn post or email click leads to the same central platform form.

[08:10] Manny Cruz | Volunteer Coordinator
We have ten fictional partner schools for testing. Each has a school ID and invitation token. Match students using their school account and normalized email. A repeat form submission through another campaign should not create another person. Never merge two different emails based only on a shared name.

[09:45] Nora James | School Partnerships Lead
I will verify each school requirement by September 30: hours required, December deadline, and whether the student seeks service hours or a capstone. Capstone eligibility needs the school’s approval; attending one event does not complete a capstone. High school profiles need guardian consent before assignment.

[11:30] Lena Brooks | Logistics Lead
I will confirm the canopies by October 9 and the E001 rain plan by October 23 with Susie. Food and decorations have not been ordered. We can ask for a quote, but nobody has accepted that task yet.

[12:40] Susie Bennett | Executive Director
Flag food and decoration quotes as unassigned with no agreed deadline. Manny should decide whether they are needed before assigning work. Do not turn a suggestion into an approved purchase.

[14:05] Manny Cruz | Volunteer Coordinator
Draft confirmations November 2, publish approved shifts November 6, and propose reminders 48 hours before each event. Capture actual check-in and checkout per shift. No-shows receive zero hours. A missing checkout leaves hours blank and pending review, not zero and not the planned shift length.

[16:00] Amina Cole | Grants and Evaluation Lead
Subtract recorded unpaid breaks. Keep calculated hours separate from approved hours. If someone leaves early, use their actual departure. Coordinator corrections need a reason and review date. Only approved hours go to school reports.

[17:30] Priya Shah | Programs Lead
For anonymous service issues, include event, time, category, what was observed, immediate staff notification, and unresolved follow-up. Example: 10:20 a.m., maternal health station ran out of size 1 diapers; one visitor left without supplies; staff lead notified. Do not record the visitor’s identity.

[19:00] Manny Cruz | Volunteer Coordinator
December 1 we can draft feedback requests; December 4 is the review meeting; school verification is due by December 11 before the December 18 student deadline. Send requests only after coordinator approval. These are plans, and attendance evidence will come from November.

[20:20] Susie Bennett | Executive Director
Confirmed logistics are distinct from pending supplies. AI task suggestions stay drafts until Manny approves them. Please keep transcript timestamps attached so he can check why each task was proposed.

End of mock transcript. Task extraction is intentionally left for the platform AI; the discussion contains confirmed decisions, commitments, tentative suggestions, and unresolved items.
